section.sectionSummaryBrief: The angels' objection to giving the Torah was not about giving it to souls, but specifically to the physical human body, as they argued it should be given to flesh and blood.
section.t: And the explanation is,
that the claim of the angels regarding the giving of the Torah to Israel was not about giving the Torah to the souls
(of Israel),
for even the angels knew that souls are on a higher level than the angels,
rather their claim was about giving the Torah to the body,
as the Gemara states,
"Do You seek to give it to flesh and blood?"
And furthermore,
even regarding the body,
their claim was not about giving the Torah to a body in general
(a spiritual body),
but about giving the Torah to the human body, which is a physical body,
as the Gemara states
(above)
"Do You seek to give it to flesh and blood?"

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The song of the angels is mentioned in prophecy because they have a body, whereas the song of the souls, which is higher, is not heard by prophets since souls have no body.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter9,
behold, we find that the song of the angels is mentioned in the Prophets,
as it is stated in the Haftarah of Shavuot,
"And I heard behind me a voice of a great rushing"10,
and it is written, "The sound of their wings was like the sound of many waters, like the sound of Shaddai"11,
"And the Ofanim and the holy Chayot with a great noise"12,
but the song of the souls is not found in the Prophets.
And this is,
that there is also a song of the souls,
for the souls have constant ascents,
as it is stated13
"They go from strength to strength,"
and as it is stated14
"And it shall be, from month to month, and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all flesh shall come,"
which is the matter of the movement and ascent of the souls, who ascend to the upper Garden of Eden and return to the lower Garden of Eden and ascend again to the upper Garden of Eden,
and it is known that every ascent is through song,
as per the statement15
"All who possess song go out with song and are drawn in with song,"
and since the ascent of the souls is higher than the ascent of the angels,
it is therefore understood that the song of the souls is also greater than the song of the angels,
and nevertheless, the song of the souls is not mentioned in the Prophets.
And the reason for this is explained in Likkutei Torah16,
because the angels possess a soul and a body,
for although they are called "separate intellects"17,
this is only in relation to the lower body,
but nevertheless, even the angels have a body,
as it is stated18
"He makes His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire,"
and the Ramban explained19
that this refers to the body of the angels.
And this is,
that it is impossible to interpret that it refers to the soul of the angels,
for in the soul of the angels, the matter of fire and spirit does not apply at all,
for although fire and spirit are two fine elements,
and in this itself, the angels are from the fineness of the elements,
as is evident from the Ramban's explanation,
nevertheless, they are elements.
And this matter does not apply to the soul of the angels,
which is the matter of the emotions of love and fear,
the camp of Michael in Chessed and the camp of Gavriel in Gevurah20,
and especially according to what is explained in Tanya21
in the name of the Zohar22
that there are intellectual angels,
for in the matter of emotions, and all the more so in the matter of intellect, the matter of even fine elements does not apply.
And it must be concluded that what is written "He makes His angels spirits" refers to the body of the angels.
And since the angels possess a body,
therefore their song is heard by the ears of the prophets.
But the song of the souls, who have no body at all,
and the matter of their song is the matter of comprehension and love and fear,
this cannot be heard by a prophet.
And just as it is regarding hearing,
so too is it regarding sight,
that the angels are perceived by sight,
as it is stated23
"And he saw, and behold, three men were standing by him,"
for since the angels have a body,
meaning that even in their standing and state they have a body,
therefore they can clothe themselves further below,
until they are perceived by sight, etc.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The angels argued that since they too have a body, the Torah could be given to them, but Moshe answered that it must be given specifically to a physical human body that can overcome the evil inclination.
section.t: And from all this it is understood that the claim of the angels regarding the giving of the Torah to Israel was not from the aspect of the soul,
for the souls are higher than the angels,
but from the aspect of the body.
And this is,
that even the angels knew that the giving of the Torah must specifically be to souls in bodies,
and nevertheless they argued that the Torah should be given to them,
for since they too possess a body,
this would also suffice for the giving of the Torah,
and there would be no need to give the Torah to a body of flesh and blood,
for from the aspect of flesh and the heat of the blood, an undesirable matter could occur, etc.
And to this they were answered,
"Have you descended to Egypt?... Is there an evil inclination among you?"
meaning that the limitations and boundaries of the bodies of the angels are not sufficient,
rather, limitations and boundaries such that the evil inclination applies to them are needed,
and even that must be transformed into good,
as per the statement of the Baal Shem Tov24
on the verse25
"Turn from evil and do good,"
that one must turn away from evil and make it into good,
and therefore the Torah was given specifically to a body of flesh and blood26.
And likewise regarding the claim of the angels at the time of the creation of the world and regarding the Mishkan
[as was explained earlier that these three matters are related to each other,
that the sustenance of the Ten Utterances
(from which the world is constantly created,
according to the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov27
on the verse28
"Forever, O Lord, Your word stands firm in the heavens,"
that the word of God must constantly be in the created being to bring it into being, to enliven it, and to sustain it),
is drawn from the Ten Commandments in the Torah,
for the Torah completes the purpose of the intention of creation, that the world should be a Sanctuary and Tabernacle for Him, blessed be He],
that their claim was that the spiritual body of the angels is sufficient.
And to this they were answered that specifically a body of flesh and blood is needed,
because,
"Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world, He created only for His glory,"
as it is stated29
"Everyone who is called by My name, and for My glory I created him, I formed him, even I made him"30,
and it is written31
"I have made the earth, and created man upon it,"
"I have made" is a term of making and perfecting32,
meaning that the purpose of creation is to perfect and elevate all of creation and to make it, through the Torah, a Sanctuary and Tabernacle for Him, blessed be He,
and for this, specifically a body of flesh and blood is needed,
for through this, even the lowest can be elevated.
And as is known the parable33
of raising a building, that one must raise it specifically from its foundation,
but if one raises it from its middle, then its foundation will not be raised.
